sources.core_claim: The Intramonth Momentum Cycle (Nathan, Suominen, Tasa 2026): US momentum returns concentrate in six trading days per month ending four trading days before month end; $1 in a value-weighted WML grows to 18.78 in those days vs 2.37 otherwise (1980-2025); loser-driven; mechanism is predictable month-end cash demand (selling losers for liquidity); the window shifted by exactly one day when SEC moved to T+1 settlement in May 2024; sector momentum D+1 positive, D+2/D+3 reversal.
sources.credibility: SSRN working paper 2026; web-search result summary only, full text not opened this round
sources.project_applicability: Published mechanism behind Leg 1/2/3 of direction C; supports a liquidity-driven, not information-driven, cycle.
sources.reflection: Single-stock evidence; the sector-ETF version is Quantpedia own extension. T+1 settlement shifted the window by one day in May 2024, so the fixed D+1/D-10..D-5 calendar of the ETF rule may be misaligned in the anchor window (recorded, rule not changed).

sources.core_claim: Untying the Knot (Burt, Duchin, Hrdlicka, SSRN 4636749, Nov 2023): 842 US dual-class firms 1965-2020; separating cash-flow and voting rights improves price informativeness; dual-class shares respond less to negative earnings surprises, carry larger short positions and show no shorting-premium anomaly. The only tradable rule in the paper is a monthly double sort (EW, FF3+MOM alpha, DiD 0.61%/mo), not a share-class price-ratio pair trade.
sources.credibility: SSRN; abstract via web search only (SSRN page returned 403 to direct fetch)
sources.project_applicability: Origin of direction A. The paper does NOT prescribe a class-vs-class price-ratio z-score trade; that construction is local, motivated by twin-stock literature.
sources.reflection: Published evidence is about informativeness and short-selling constraints across firms, not about mean reversion of the price ratio within a firm; the direction-level premise is therefore weak.

sources.core_claim: Yang (South African Journal of Business Management 2025): GOOGL/GOOG spread modelled as an OU process 2015-2024 shows statistically significant twin-stock arbitrage profits (expected returns 8.71%-8.36%, Sharpe 5.4-5.6 under a stated transaction cost of 0.001 per year, robust to RDS.A/RDS.B), half-life about 4.8 days, no shorting-cost or borrow modelling visible.
sources.credibility: Peer-reviewed regional journal, full text opened; cost model implausibly light, Sharpe of 5+ is not credible as tradable
sources.project_applicability: Only public evidence that a same-firm class spread mean reverts (GOOG/GOOGL, 2015-2024); motivates a z-score pair on daily closes.
sources.reflection: Half-life of ~5 days means a monthly or weekly rebalanced z-score trade is much slower than the paper OU horizon; a 0.001 cost is not comparable to 5-10 bp per side per leg.

sources.core_claim: Hobby repo: XLK vs its 24 largest constituents, free Yahoo daily data 2015-present, Granger causality says ETF leads; default reversion book (ETF up -> short constituents, ETF down -> long) with a one-bar hold, shock gate = top tercile of trailing ETF returns, Sharpe about 1.2-1.3 (0.9 ungated), costs charged on turnover in bps (level not stated), borrow costs ignored; momentum mirror loses money; the book is directional (net market exposure reported).
sources.credibility: Repo README opened and saved; single author, no independent replication, no borrow cost, one-day hold implies daily turnover
sources.project_applicability: Origin of direction B. The repo tests a daily-turnover directional book; this iteration tests the low-turnover market-neutral variant (5/10 day hold, k laggard constituents vs short ETF).
sources.reflection: A one-bar hold with full daily turnover is exactly the shape that failed on costs in T-20260929-32 (gap fade); low-turnover reversion after ETF crashes may keep only the multi-day tail of the effect.

sources.core_claim: Ben-David, Franzoni, Moussawi (JF 2018, "Do ETFs Increase Volatility?"): ETF ownership raises stock daily volatility and negative autocorrelation of stock prices; the lead-lag relation is induced by early price discovery in the ETF market and plays out within the daily lag.
sources.credibility: Peer-reviewed; web-search summary only, full text not opened
sources.project_applicability: Published support that ETF-to-constituent effects resolve within about a day, i.e. a 5-10 day hold captures at most a small tail.
sources.reflection: Effect is intraday/daily; a multi-day hold is a test of persistence, not of the published mechanism.

sources.core_claim: Hou (RFS 2007): the big-firm to small-firm lead-lag effect is intra-industry, driven by slow diffusion of industry information and sluggish reaction to negative news; stronger in smaller, less-followed industries.
sources.project_applicability: Prior that lead-lag is stronger among small, slow names; the fixed mega-cap constituent list here is the weakest case for it.
sources.reflection: Fixed list of the ten largest 2016 holdings is the opposite of the small/slow names in which Hou finds the effect; expected weak.
